subject: DPA: subprocessor notification sequencing and objection window
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@arcadia-systems.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Nguyen <procurement@arcadia-systems.com>, Ben Clark <bclark@evans-law.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA & subprocessors - initial materials

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the packet. We received your DPA draft and the initial subprocessor list — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few things procurement/legal flagged on our side:

- Subprocessor notification window: Arcadia requires a 60-day notice for new subprocessors so we can run our vendor risk checks and schedule any necessary audits.
- Objection process: we need a clearly defined escalation path and a right to pause onboarding if there are unresolved security concerns.
- Audit rights: for any subprocessors handling PHI or highly sensitive telemetry, Arcadia requires evidence of SOC2 Type II or a compensating control review before onboarding.

Attached: Arcadia_Security_Questionnaire.pdf with specific baseline checks.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept a 60-day rolling notification or suggest alternatives? Also please share your preferred execution flow (DocuSign timeline) once redlines are settled.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Procurement
Arcadia Systems

(Attachment: Arcadia_Security_Questionnaire.pdf)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@arcadia-systems.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & subprocessors - initial materials

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura and Naomi from legal/privacy and Dev for the subproc ops perspective.

Quick summary of what we can do and a proposed compromise:

- Notification window: Redwood's standard practice is a 30–45 day notification window depending on the criticality of the processor. For non-sensitive infra we typically use 30 days; for anything touching regulated data we use 45 days.
- Objection process: we propose an objection period tied to the notification window (i.e., objection must be raised within the window with clear remediation requests). If unresolved, it escalates to legal (cc: Laura), then to senior sponsor for a final decision.
- Emergency onboarding: for critical security patching or emergency failover, we can permit an expedited path with documented mitigations and retrospective evidence.

Attachments: I attached our current redline (Arcadia_DPA_redline_v1.docx) and the subprocessor CSV export so you can see the population. If Arcadia would accept 45 days for processors handling regulated data and 30 for the rest, that would balance procurement needs and our operational cadence.

If that sounds like a path, I can ask Laura to draft the change language and we can route a final to DocuSign for execution.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday to align?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(Attachments: Arcadia_DPA_redline_v1.docx, subprocessor_list_20270315.csv)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA & subprocessors - proposed language

Hi Samantha / Jordan — Laura from Legal. I reviewed the v1 redline and proposed focused language that should map directly into the DPA and the subprocessor notice addendum:

Key proposed edits (high-level):
- Notification window: Replace a blanket 60-day request with a two-tier window in Section 3.2: 45 days for subprocessors that process regulated data (PII/PHI) and 30 days for other subprocessors.
- Quiet acceptance: If no objection is raised within the applicable notice window, the subprocessor will be deemed accepted. This avoids indefinite holds.
- Objection mechanics: Objections must be submitted in writing specifying the grounds and proposed remediation. Parties will use a 15-business-day remediation period before invoking any pause/right to block.
- Emergency exceptions: Add a carve-out for emergency security or availability needs with an expedited 5-business-day notification plus mandatory post-onboarding evidence and compensating controls.
- Audit evidence: For subprocessors flagged by Arcadia as high-risk, require SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, or a controlled onboarding with documented compensating controls.

I attached a short playbook (see link in the DPA doc) with escalation steps and a template notice email for your procurement team. If Arcadia can accept the two-tier window + emergency carve-out we can take the v3 redline to DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

(Internal note to Jordan/Naomi/Dev: we'll track objections in the legal tracker and flag any vendor that requires remediation. Naomi, can you confirm the SOC2 gating threshold?)

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@arcadia-systems.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Nguyen <procurement@arcadia-systems.com>, Ben Clark <bclark@evans-law.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & subprocessors - proposed language

Thanks Laura — that structure is helpful. A few clarifications from Arcadia's side:

- We cannot accept any 'quiet acceptance' for processors that will handle telemetry and aggregated usage data used in billing/analytics. For those, we require affirmative sign-off (Procurement) after review — no deemed acceptance.
- The 5-business-day emergency carve-out is reasonable but we need a clear list of what qualifies as "emergency" (security breach, PII/PHI exposure, region-wide availability incident).
- Audit evidence: Arcadia will accept SOC 2 Type II OR an in-person/remote vendor review within 30 days of onboarding if the vendor doesn't have SOC2.

If Redwood can add an explicit exception to quiet acceptance for analytics/billing processors and include a short definition of emergencies, Arcadia is comfortable with the 45/30 tiering and the 5-day expedited path. Once language is updated we can route to Ben Clark on our side and get the DocuSign link queued.

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Procurement
Arcadia Systems

(Attachment: none)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, Tom Nguyen <procurement@arcadia-systems.com>, Ben Clark <bclark@evans-law.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: agreed sequencing & next steps (DocuSign ready)

Hi all — thanks for the rapid back-and-forth. Per Laura's edits and Samantha's clarifications we've agreed on the following compromise to include in the DPA redline v3:

1) Two-tier notification window: 45 days for subprocessors handling regulated data (PII/PHI), 30 days for others.
2) Quiet acceptance allowed except for processors designated by Arcadia for billing/analytics (those require affirmative procurement sign-off).
3) Objection process: written objection during the applicable notice window; 15-business-day remediation period; legal escalation if unresolved.
4) Emergency exception: defined as (a) confirmed security breach affecting Arcadia data, (b) critical regional availability incident impacting >25% of Arcadia traffic, or (c) urgent regulatory requirement. Emergency onboarding allowed with 5-business-day post-notice documentation and mandatory retrospective evidence.
5) Audit evidence: SOC2 Type II preferred; if absent, allow a vendor review within 30 days post-onboarding.

I've attached Arcadia_DPA_redline_v3.docx with tracked changes that incorporate these bullets. If Arcadia confirms the language, I'll send the DocuSign envelope (link below) and propose a signing window of 5 business days to keep the timeline tight.
